summary: Configured node1's kernel to boot with audit=1 persistently by using grubby --update-kernel=ALL --args="audit=1", which updated both BLS boot entries (the default kernel and the rescue entry). Restarted node1 via systemctl reboot to prove persistence, confirmed the boot ID changed (real reboot, not just a service bounce), and verified /proc/cmdline and auditctl -s both show audit=1/enabled=1 post-reboot.
actions_performed: Inspected current boot entries and cmdline via grubby --info=ALL and /proc/cmdline
Ran `sudo grubby --update-kernel=ALL --args="audit=1"` to add audit=1 to all boot loader entries
Verified audit=1 appears in grubby --info=ALL output and in /boot/loader/entries/*.conf for both entries
Captured pre-reboot boot_id and uptime baseline
Issued `sudo systemctl reboot` in background so the acknowledgement returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again (connection timed out, then reset, then succeeded)
Verified post-reboot boot_id differs from baseline, confirming an actual restart
Verified /proc/cmdline contains audit=1 and `auditctl -s` reports enabled 1 post-reboot

evidence.requirement: audit=1 persistently configured in bootloader for all kernel entries
evidence.summary: grubby --update-kernel=ALL --args="audit=1" applied; grubby --info=ALL and grep of BLS entry files confirm audit=1 present in both the default kernel entry and the rescue entry
Captured baseline boot_id (f455a75c-ec12-49a8-a647-c2be3f67c08c) and uptime before restart

evidence.requirement: Node restart acknowledgement returns before disconnect
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot issued in background; command returned pid immediately

evidence.requirement: Poll until node1 command execution available again
evidence.summary: Probe commands show connection timed out, then reset by peer (node cycling), then succeeded once back up

evidence.requirement: Proof boot identity changed and audit=1 active post-restart
evidence.summary: Post-reboot boot_id (f54417d4-b275-4ae8-b1c7-0d7cdfc60035) differs from baseline, confirming real restart; /proc/cmdline includes audit=1 and auditctl -s reports enabled 1, proving the kernel booted with audit=1 and the setting persisted
